newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London maintained early gains and prices ended firmer. The second month-March contract last traded $1.50 higher at $305.50. However, sentiment remains bearish due to lack of substantial physical offtake and forecasts of another surplus in 1996/97. In New York raw sugar futures ended with modest gains in a technical reaction to recent losses. However, the market was unable to punch through major chart resistance. In spite of today's correction, bearish fundamentals will continue to weigh on sentiment.

PAKISTAN - According to the private Pakistan Sugar Mills Association 250,000-300,000 tonnes of white sugar will be imported between May and November 1997. It added that sugar production in 1995/96 (July/June) reached 2.47 million tonnes, white value, 130,000 tonnes short of the total estimated domestic demand of 2.6 million tonnes. However, it is not entirely clear whether the demand estimate contains illegal exports.

JAMAICA - Sugar production in April 1996 amounted to 39,300 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 36,516 tonnes. This brought cumulative production in the first half of 1995/96 (November/April) up to 161,935 tonnes compared to 147,495 tonnes the corresponding period the previous year. Total production 1994/95 reached 211,539 tonnes against 220,350 tonnes in 1993/94 and 224,015 tonnes in 1992/93.

BANGLADESH - Sugar production in January 1996 amounted to 48,651 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 53,189 tonnes. This brought cumulative production in the first four months of 1995/96 (October/January) up to 124,879 tonnes compared to 145,502 tonnes in October/January 1994/95. Total production in 1994/95 reached 293,630 tonnes against 240,600 tonnes in 1993/94 and 203,786 tonnes in 1992/93.

PORTUGAL - Sugar imports in July 1996 amounted to 44,345 tonnes, raw value, against 51 tonnes in July 1995. This brought cumulative imports in the first seven months of 1996 (January/July) up to 184,104 tonnes against 192,935 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total imports in 1995 reached 312,542 tonnes against 340,710 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of origin in January/July 1996 were Swaziland with 42,699 tonnes raws against 28,123 tonnes, Zimbabwe with 33,570 tonnes compared to 19,939 tonnes and Jamaica with 30,894 tonnes against nil. Sugar exports in January/July 1996 amounted to 10,563 tonnes, up from last year's 5,746 tonnes. Total exports in 1995 amounted to 15,432 tonnes against 7,434 tonnes in 1994. The major country of destination in January/July 1996 was Spain with 7,848 tonnes whites against 2,389 tonnes.

UNITED STATES - Sugar imports under the 1996/97 (October/September) tariff rate quota up to November 3, 1996 amounted to 81,259 tonnes, raw value. This is equivalent to 3.75 percent of the total quota of 2.17 million tonnes.
